title: Interfaces
description: Interfaces, classes, and polymorphism in C#

exercises.title: Define Interface
exercises.description: Define interface Shape with Area() double method. Implement for Rectangle. Create rect = Rectangle{Width: 3, Height: 4}. Print Area().
exercises.starter_code:
// interface Shape

record Rectangle(double Width, double Height);
hints: Define `interface IShape { double Area(); }` and implement explicitly on concrete types.
Program against the abstraction (`IShape`) where polymorphism clarifies intent.

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define Writer interface with write bytes. Implement for Logger with fmt.FConsole.WriteLineln. Create Logger and call Write.
hints: Byte counts often come from `.Length`; pair with ASCII/UTF8 encodings as needed.
Return `int`/`void` signatures should mirror exercise stubs.

exercises.title: Multiple Implementations
exercises.description: Define Shape interface with Area() double. Implement for both Circle (with Radius) and Rectangle. Create Circle{5} and Rectangle{3,4}, call Area on both, Console.WriteLine the larger area.
hints: `Math.PI` supplies double precision for circular areas.
Compare polymorphic `.Area()` results with standard relational operators.

exercises.title: Type Assertion
exercises.description: Define Describable interface with Describe() string. Implement for Person{name}. Create interface var, use type assertion to get Person and Console.WriteLine name.
exercises.starter_code:
record Person(string Name) : IDescribable { public string Describe() => "Person: " + Name; }
interface IDescribable { string Describe(); }
hints: Downcast deliberately with `(Person)obj` once you trust runtime type.
Pattern matching `switch` alternatives also unwrap derived data.

exercises.title: Type Switch
exercises.description: Create a function describeAny(x Object) that uses type switch to Console.WriteLine "int: <value>" for int, "string: <value>" for string, "unknown" for other types. Test with both an int and a string.
exercises.starter_code:
// describeAny(42); describeAny("hello");

static void DescribeAny(object x) { }
hints: Use recursive `switch (obj)` patterns for `case int`, `case string`, etc.

exercises.title: Interface with Slice
exercises.description: Define interface Speaker with Speak() string. Implement for Dog (returns "Woaf") and Cat (returns "Mew"). Create a slice of Speaker with one Dog and one Cat, then call Speak on each.
hints: Loop and print each `.Speak()` return value sequentially.

exercises.title: Empty Interface
exercises.description: Create a slice of empty Object containing: the int 42, the string "hello", and the float 3.14. Print each one's concrete type using a type switch.
hints: Floating literals are `double`; some checkers prefix them with `float64:` in stdout.
Enumerate with `foreach` plus `switch` patterns on each boxed item.
